empty-name.message: A file name can't be empty.
empty-name.description: Error when a file is added or renamed with no name.

path-separator.message: File names can't contain a slash or a backslash: “{{name}}”.
path-separator.description: Error when a file name contains a slash or a backslash. {{name}} is the file name as typed.

invalid-character.message: “{{name}}” contains a character that isn't allowed in a file name.
invalid-character.description: Error when a file name contains a character the operating systems don't allow, such as a colon or a control character. {{name}} is the file name as typed.

unsupported-extension.message: Electron Fiddle can't open “{{name}}”, because its file type isn't supported.
unsupported-extension.description: Error when a file name doesn't end in a type the app supports, such as .js, .html or .json. {{name}} is the file name as typed.

reserved-name.message: “{{name}}” is a reserved name and can't be used for a file.
reserved-name.description: Error when a file name is one the app or the operating system reserves, such as package.json or a Windows device name. {{name}} is the file name as typed.

duplicate-name.description: Error when a file is added or renamed to a name another file already has. {{name}} is the file name.

second-main-entry.message: This fiddle already has a main file, so “{{name}}” can't be another one.
second-main-entry.description: Error when a second main file (main.js, main.cjs or main.mjs) is added. {{name}} is the file name as typed.

no-main-entry.message: “{{name}}” is the main file and has to stay one.
no-main-entry.description: Error when the main file is renamed to a name that isn't a main file name. {{name}} is the current file name.

remove-main-entry.message: “{{name}}” is the main file and can't be removed.
remove-main-entry.description: Error when someone tries to remove the fiddle's main file. {{name}} is the file name.

file-not-found.description: Error when an action names a file the fiddle doesn't have. {{name}} is the file name.

folder-not-found.description: Error when a fiddle folder to open no longer exists. {{path}} is the folder's path; keep it as it is.

no-supported-files.message: There are no files here that Electron Fiddle can open.
no-supported-files.description: Error when a folder, gist or example has no files of a supported type.

invalid-json.description: Error when a JSON file can't be read. {{file}} is the file name, such as package.json; keep it as it is.

missing-package-json.message: Packaging needs a package.json file, and this fiddle doesn't have one.
missing-package-json.description: Error when a fiddle is packaged without a package.json. package.json is a file name; keep it as it is.

invalid-name.description: Error when a module is added under a name npm doesn't allow. {{name}} is the name as typed. npm is a product name.

invalid-spec.message: “{{spec}}” isn't a version npm can install for {{name}}. Use a version number, a version range or a tag.
invalid-spec.description: Error when a module's version is a Git URL, a path or something else npm could fetch from anywhere. {{spec}} is the version as typed, {{name}} the package name. npm is a product name.

command-not-started.description: Error when the package manager can't be started, for example because it isn't installed. {{command}} is the command, such as npm; keep it as it is. {{detail}} is the operating system's own explanation, in English.

install-failed.description: Error when npm or Yarn ends with a failure while installing a fiddle's modules. {{packageManager}} is npm or yarn; keep it as it is. {{exit}} is the exit code, or the name of the signal that ended it.

registry-metadata.message: The npm registry sent unexpected information about {{name}}.
registry-metadata.description: Error when the npm registry's answer for a package isn't in the expected form. {{name}} is the package name. npm is a product name.

example-not-found.description: Error when a link or command names a built-in example that doesn't exist. {{name}} is the name as given.

invalid-path.description: Error when the path of an example from the Electron documentation has empty or relative segments. {{path}} is the path as given; keep it as it is.

invalid-tag.message: Couldn't tell which Electron version “{{tag}}” belongs to.
invalid-tag.description: Error when the Git tag of an example from the Electron documentation isn't a release tag, such as v30.0.0. {{tag}} is the tag as given; keep it as it is.

template-status.message: Couldn't download the template: the server answered with HTTP {{status}}.
template-status.description: Error when the download of the starter template fails with an error status. {{status}} is the HTTP status code, such as 500; keep it as it is.

template-unreachable.message: Couldn't download the template. Check your internet connection.
template-unreachable.description: Error when the starter template can't be downloaded, usually because the computer is offline.

rate-limited.message: GitHub's rate limit was reached. Try again in a few minutes.
rate-limited.description: Error when GitHub refuses requests because too many were sent. GitHub is a product name.

github-response.description: Error when GitHub answers with an error status and no explanation. {{status}} is the HTTP status code, such as 500; keep it as it is. GitHub is a product name.

github-response-detail.description: Error when GitHub answers with an error status and an explanation. {{status}} is the HTTP status code, such as 404; keep it as it is. {{detail}} is GitHub's own explanation, in English. GitHub is a product name.

timeout.description: Error when a request to GitHub takes too long. GitHub is a product name.

unreachable.message: Couldn't reach GitHub. Check your internet connection.
unreachable.description: Error when GitHub can't be reached, usually because the computer is offline. GitHub is a product name.

unexpected-response.message: GitHub sent a response that couldn't be read.
unexpected-response.description: Error when GitHub's answer isn't in the expected form. GitHub is a product name.

too-many-files.message: A gist can have at most {{max}} files.
too-many-files.description: Error when a fiddle has more files than a GitHub gist can hold. {{max}} is the limit, such as 300. Gist is GitHub's name for a shared snippet.

file-too-large.message: “{{name}}” is larger than {{maxMb}} MB, the most a gist file can hold.
file-too-large.description: Error when a file is too big for a GitHub gist. {{name}} is the file name, {{maxMb}} the limit in megabytes, such as 10. Gist is GitHub's name for a shared snippet.
